govdocs-archive_org-OperationNorthwoodsU: Secker’s Northwoods sheaf — the full lot — strings the freed 1962 papers. The high brass’s false-flag rede — to warrant Cuba war — stands here whole. Kennedy spurned the rede. The papers came to light in 1997. The sheaf is the whole first-hand hoard.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-HandwritingExpe: This item — Handwriting Experts — is a National Security Internet Archive file. The file’s full context is unclear. Its subject seems to be the JFK case. Experts studied the disputed writings. Archivists value such fragments. The item is a fragment of the archive.
medieval-europe: Historian H. W. C. Davis surveys a thousand years of European history, from the fall of Rome to the dawn of the Renaissance. Kings and popes, crusades and universities, peasants and knights all take their place in a clear narrative of how medieval civilization rose, flourished, and changed. Written as a student text, it offers a solid first map of the Middle Ages.
memoir-of-father-vincent-de-paul-religio: This memoir tells the life of Father Vincent de Paul, a monk of the austere Trappist order at La Trappe. His story of prayer, labor, and silence offers a window into one of Catholicism's most demanding spiritual paths. Reverent and edifying, it preserves the memory of a holy life.
our-hundred-days-in-europe: Oliver Wendell Holmes, the Autocrat of the Breakfast Table, recounts his hundred days in Europe — his triumphant return to the land of his fathers. His wit and warmth charmed two continents. A delightful travel memoir. Oxford honors and Stratford pilgrimages crown his happy journey.
the-real-dope: Ring Lardner's Real Dope gathers his baseball stories in their original dugout slang — the national game as only Lardner could tell it. His cheerfully illiterate narrators speak immortal American comedy. The funniest sports writing in the language. Baseball fans treasure these tales as the game's truest comedy.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-agape: A 1913 entry on the agape — the love-feasts of the early Christians. Henri Leclercq traces their rise and fall. Bread and charity joined the Eucharist. Abuses ended the custom. Fellowship's feast in the infant Church. Tertullian praised their simple charity.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alexander-pop: This 1913 reference article on Alexander Pope — the great Catholic poet of England. Patrick Lennox honors his verse and faith. The Rape of the Lock still delights. His couplets ruled an age. The little man of Twickenham, immortal. His grotto at Twickenham drew the curious.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antipope: A 1913 entry on the antipope — the rival claimant to Peter's chair. The entry surveys the long sad list. Schism, not heresy, made their claim. The Church survived them all. The shadow beside the true line. Their names fill the history's margins.
